rationale.overall: B and A share the same composition and geometry, but B's slab and ground read as a single coherently lit object while A carries blotchy olive-tinted smudges and a stray dark rectangular patch on the slab's top face that break the illusion of a solid material.
rationale.material: REF's slab is matte stone with mottling that follows its form; B's smoother gradient with a subtle top-face highlight band and clean bevel transition conveys volume more convincingly, whereas A's mottling sits on the surface as flat discoloration rather than grain, and A's harsh, sharply-drawn background scratch lines diverge more from REF's fine, softly-lit floor striation than B's finer woven grain does.
rationale.silhouette: The two takes have effectively identical outer shapes — same slab wedge, ribbon loop, glow line and diagonal floor break — with no discernible edge or proportion advantage either way.
rationale.smallsize: At 128px, 32px and 16px both collapse to the same dark diagonal bar with an orange under-edge against a warm split ground, and neither the artifacts on A nor the finer grain on B survive the downscale to differentiate the read.
